facts.fact: The National Payment Systems Act, 2022 (Act 8 of 2022), assented to 2 June 2022 and published in Gazette 43, commenced on 23 June 2022 and repealed the Payments Systems Act 2009.

The National Payment Systems Act, 2022 (s.6) bars any person from providing payment services or operating a system without a Bank of Sierra Leone licence and sets e-money issuer conditions, while s.8 exempts only banks and financial institutions from needing a new licence; s.5 seats mobile money operators and the Fintech Association on the National Payment System Committee. Date is the Act's commencement.

note: No fact on connection: s.16 requires objective, non-discriminatory access rules for systems but sets no duty on providers to connect to each other or a switch.

facts.fact: Bank of Sierra Leone National Switch Directives issued December 2024 require all commercial banks and mobile money operators to process instant, card and POS transactions through the national switch SaPS from 1 April 2025.
NatCA states the Bank of Sierra Leone regulates mobile money operators under Section 2 of the National Payment Systems Act 2022, alongside a Draft Non-Bank Led Mobile Money Regulation of 2024.

note: Draft Non-Bank Led Mobile Money Regulation 2024 noted as draft; non-bank licensing not stated.

facts.fact: The Bank of Sierra Leone announced on 10 April 2025 that all financial institutions and fintechs, mandated to route all domestic transactions through the National Switch, now have until 30 June 2025 instead of 31 March 2025 to integrate.
